overview: Ayambil is a significant fasting practice in Jainism, primarily observed by devotees seeking spiritual purification and discipline. It is characterized by consuming only one meal a day, devoid of any spices, oil, or dairy products. The practice is seen as a form of tapasya (austerity) aimed at reducing karma and fostering self-control. Ayambil is typically observed during certain religious periods, such as Paryushana, and can be practiced for a single day or extended periods. The fast is often accompanied by religious activities like prayer, meditation, and scriptural study. In Jainism, Ayambil is highly revered as it promotes simplicity, non-attachment, and physical and mental purification.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: Austerity is the purification of the soul by the attenuation of karma that obscures knowledge and perception.
primary_sources.notes: This text provides a foundational understanding of the role of austerity in Jain practice, highlighting the spiritual goals of fasting such as Ayambil.

misconceptions.myth: Ayambil is meant to cause physical suffering.
misconceptions.reality: The purpose of Ayambil is not to cause suffering but to cultivate discipline and control over desires, leading to spiritual growth and detachment from material comforts.
